hypothesis: A generic profit floor and trailing stop activated before HYPE's eight-hour soft boundary may retain more after-cost profit than the active no-target contract.
decision: Reject the frozen 25/15/10, 40/15/20, and 60/15/30 bps activation/floor/trail policies for canonical HYPE. Preserve their telemetry as negative mechanism evidence and do not apply them to the current open lifecycle or a future profile. This rejection is limited to these exact policies.
falsifier: A prospectively frozen pre-soft profit-protection policy that improves actual after-cost exits across multiple non-adjacent profile-matched live windows without increasing loss concentration would update this rejection; changed source-prefix hashes would invalidate the present audit.
limitations: Six live HYPE closes remain sparse and span non-independent process windows.
Completed one-minute bars cannot reconstruct intraminute trigger ordering.
Counterfactual fills reuse measured exit friction rather than submitted orders.
The negative historical control does not establish that canonical HYPE entries are durable.
Rejecting these exact policies does not reject every possible profit-protection design.
